sources.entry: Streaming media is multimedia that is delivered and consumed in a continuous manner from a source, with little or no intermediate storage in network elements.

summary.name: Streaming media
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article explaining streaming media: the delivery of multimedia over a network in a continuous stream for real-time or near real-time playback, covering its history, technology, and business trends.
use_cases: Understanding how streaming differs from file downloading
Researching the history of online video and audio streaming
Learning about live versus on-demand streaming methods
Studying the streaming wars and subscription service competition
Background reading on music streaming and the decline of DVD rentals
summary.what_it_does: The article defines streaming media as multimedia delivered through a network and rendered in real-time or near real-time, contrasting it with file downloading. It describes streaming over the internet as well as local-network and Bluetooth use. It traces history from precursors such as the Théâtrophone and Muzak through early 1990s and 1990s pioneers like RealNetworks and Microsoft to YouTube and the streaming wars. It also explains live streaming (true streaming) versus on-demand streaming (progressive download), and covers the impact on DVD rental and music industries, including Napster.
notable: Covers history from early telemetry and Théâtrophone through RealNetworks, QuickTime, and YouTube
Explains live streaming (true streaming) versus on-demand progressive download
Discusses the streaming wars and the shift from DVD rentals to streaming
